In order to see specific help about any specific command, please use the 'man' command. Use 'man man' to see more about the man command. To see a full list of all commands, use 'all-commands'.
mono-targets
Various commands may show a mono-target in their command signature.
This means they are not static commands, and instead requires instance(s) of the class in order to invoke the command.
Each mono-target works differently as follows:
 - single: uses the first instance of the type found in the scene
 - all: uses all instances of the type found in the scene
 - registry: uses all instances of the type found in the registry
 - singleton: creates and manages a single instance automatically
The registry is a part of the Quantum Registry that allows you to decide which specific instances of the class should be used when invoking the command. In order to add an object to the registry, either use QFSW.QC.QuantumRegistry.RegisterObject<T> or the runtime command 'register-object<T>'.WelcomeNotificationWelsh (United Kingdom)WheatWhen called from '{0}', rewriting a node of type '{1}' must return a non-null value of the same type. Welcome to Quantum Console! In order to see specific help about any specific command, please use the 'man' command. Use 'man man' to see more about the man command. To see a full list of all commands, use 'all-commands'.
mono-targets
Various commands may show a mono-target in their command signature.
This means they are not static commands, and instead requires instance(s) of the class in order to invoke the command.
Each mono-target works differently as follows:
 - single: uses the first instance of the type found in the scene
 - all: uses all instances of the type found in the scene
 - registry: uses all instances of the type found in the registry
 - singleton: creates and manages a single instance automatically
The registry is a part of the Quantum Registry that allows you to decide which specific instances of the class should be used when invoking the command. In order to add an object to the registry, either use QFSW.QC.QuantumRegistry.RegisterObject<T> or the runtime command 'register-object<T>'.

Odin's custom serialization protocol is stable and fast. It is built to be fast, reliable and resilient above all.
*Words of caution* 
However, caveats apply - there is a reason Unity chose such a drastically limited serialization protocol. It keeps things simple and manageable, and limits how much complexity you can introduce into your data structures. It can be very easy to get carried away and shoot yourself in the foot when all limitations suddenly disappear, and hence we have included this cautionary warning.
Warning words aside, there can of course be valid reasons to use a more powerful serialization protocol such as Odin's. However, we advise you to use it wisely and with restraint. After all, with great power comes great responsibility!
In 2018.3, Unity introduced a new prefab workflow, and in so doing, changed how all prefabs fundamentally work. Despite our best efforts, we have so far been unable to achieve a stable implementation of Odin-serialized prefab modifications on prefab instances and variants in the new prefab workflow.This has nothing to do with Odin serializer itself, which remains rock solid. Odin-serialized ScriptableObjects and non-prefab Components/Behaviours are still perfectly stable - you are only seeing this message because this is an Odin-serialized prefab asset or instance.
Using prefabs with Odin serialization in 2018.3 and above is considered a *deprecated feature* and is officially unsupported. In short, if you disregard this message and then experience issues, we will not be able to help or support you.

harvestFestival
Jtrue: force the Harvest Festival open (HARVEST_FESTIVAL_ACTIVE, saved) and override HARVEST_FESTIVAL_KEY to DEV_TEST (not saved). false: simulate the event having ended - closes it even if the real window is open (until true or an app restart), removes the festival quests, sends you back to area04 if you are in the festival map, and removes the Kenek Bus. Progress flags are kept; use harvestFestivalReset to wipe them.U
,harvestFestivalCostume
tUnlock and immediately equip the Harvest Festival costume.U
0harvestFestivalFtueStage
Jump the Harvest Festival FTUE to a stage: 0 = arrived, minigame not done; 1 = minigame done, report-back to Mbah Wongso due; 2 = report-back done (daily loop). Also fixes up the FTUE quest and repaints the orchard.U
>harvestFestivalCompleteMinigame
>Simulate finishing the orchard minigame (runs the same completion hook the real minigame will call): stamps today done, repaints the orchard, then auto-plays the FTUE report-back (first run) or Mbah Wongso's daily thank-you line. Run it in the HarvestFestival scene to see the follow-up.U
4harvestFestivalGoldenFruit
xFire the Harvest Festival Golden Fruit finale cutscene (Scene 8) for testing 
 the real Golden Fruit grant isn't wired yet. Requires the FTUE report-back to be done and not already seen.U
,harvestFestivalOrchard
Set the orchard plots' look in HarvestFestival: true = today's minigame done (trees hidden, soil seeded/wet), false = not done (weekday trees shown). Stamps/clears HARVEST_FESTIVAL_EVENT_TICK and repaints immediately.U
2harvestFestivalOrchardDay
Preview a weekday's tree sprite in the orchard without waiting for the real day: 0=Sun Apple, 1=Mon Orange, 2=Tue Grape, 3=Wed Mango, 4=Thu Pineapple, 5=Fri Durian, 6=Sat Watermelon. Use -1 to go back to the real day. Not saved.U
,harvestFestivalNextDay
dSimulate the Harvest Festival daily reset: moves the orchard clock forward 1 day (stack it for more), so today's minigame resets, the trees come back with the next weekday's fruit, and Mbah Wongso offers 'Mulai Panen' again. FTUE flags are untouched. Not saved - restarting the app returns to the real day.U
,harvestFestivalRealDay
Undo harvestFestivalNextDay: put the orchard clock back on the real day.U
0harvestFestivalStartDate
Override the Harvest Festival start date (HARVEST_FESTIVAL_START_DATE): yyyy-MM-dd, 'today' for the current orchard day, 'none' to simulate ops removing the date from remote config (counts as the event being over: festival quests removed and you're sent home on the next scene load), or -1 to go back to remote config. Not saved. Re-enter the scene to respawn the extra NPCs.U
*harvestFestivalLength
\Override the Harvest Festival length in days (HARVEST_FESTIVAL_LENGTH): 1 or more, or -1 to go back to remote config. Not saved. Re-enter the scene to respawn the extra NPCs.U
0harvestFestivalShopReset
Clear every Mbah Surti exchange-shop limit: the per-event buy counts and the event key they belong to, the Wedang Ronde one-time purchase, and ownership of the Harvest Festival costume. Use it to re-test the caps without a fresh save.U
(harvestFestivalReset
Wipe Harvest Festival progress back to 'never touched it': all event flags, the daily + reward stamps, the debug day offset, and the invite / trigger / minigame quests. The event window and the shop are left alone (see harvestFestival, harvestFestivalShopReset). Run inside the festival map and you are bussed back to area04 first.U
@harvestFestivalMinigameSkipPhase
Orchard minigame only: finish the current phase (Harvest / Plant / Water) as if every remaining plot was done, so it fades to the next phase - run it on Water to end the round. Does nothing outside a running minigame round. Skipped plots give no Golden Fruit.U

 Warning messages
<Click to show warning message.
Odin's custom serialization protocol is stable and fast. It is built to be fast, reliable and resilient above all.
*Words of caution* 
However, caveats apply - there is a reason Unity chose such a drastically limited serialization protocol. It keeps things simple and manageable, and limits how much complexity you can introduce into your data structures. It can be very easy to get carried away and shoot yourself in the foot when all limitations suddenly disappear, and hence we have included this cautionary warning.
Warning words aside, there can of course be valid reasons to use a more powerful serialization protocol such as Odin's. However, we advise you to use it wisely and with restraint. After all, with great power comes great responsibility!U
<Click to show warning message.
In 2018.3, Unity introduced a new prefab workflow, and in so doing, changed how all prefabs fundamentally work. Despite our best efforts, we have so far been unable to achieve a stable implementation of Odin-serialized prefab modifications on prefab instances and variants in the new prefab workflow.This has nothing to do with Odin serializer itself, which remains rock solid. Odin-serialized ScriptableObjects and non-prefab Components/Behaviours are still perfectly stable - you are only seeing this message because this is an Odin-serialized prefab asset or instance.
Using prefabs with Odin serialization in 2018.3 and above is considered a *deprecated feature* and is officially unsupported. In short, if you disregard this message and then experience issues, we will not be able to help or support you.
Please keep all this in mind, if you wish to continue using Odin-serialized prefabs.U
BEnabling this will hide all warning messages that will show up in the inspector when the OdinSerialize attribute potentially does not achieve the desired effect.U
Hide Non-Serialized SerializeField/ShowInInspector Warning Messages
\Enabling this will hide all warning messages that show up when the SerializeField and the ShowInInspector attributes are used together on non-serialized fields or properties.U
